findings.title: Oversized animated GIFs can lose all but their first frame
findings.body: This passes `allow_animated_thumbnails` to the upload downsize operation, but that setting controls thumbnail generation, not whether an uploaded animation should be preserved. When it is false, `downsize_instructions` uses ImageMagick with `#{from}[0]`, which processes only the first frame. Any oversized animated GIF is therefore replaced by a static image when the tempfile is overwritten, causing irreversible loss of the animation.

findings.title: The client-side limit ignores the configured attachment size
findings.body: This replaces the type-specific `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` limit with a fixed 10 MB limit for every upload. Sites that configure attachments above 10 MB will now reject otherwise valid files in the browser before they reach the server; sites with lower limits also receive an inaccurate client-side error threshold. Keep the attachment limit configurable while allowing the intended larger image uploads.
